title: How to Check the DPI of a PDF (Free and Easy Ways) | Legenddary's SparkPrep
h1: How to check the DPI of a PDF before you print your book
description: Three plain-English ways to check the resolution of the pictures inside a PDF: simple math, Adobe Acrobat's Object Inspector, and a whole-book check. Plus the Word setting that quietly lowers your DPI.
platforms: Any PDF for Amazon KDP, IngramSpark or Lulu
lead: A PDF doesn't have one DPI. Every picture inside it has its own. Here's how to find out whether yours are sharp enough for print (300 DPI), with free and paid options.

answer.q: How do I check the DPI of a PDF?
answer.a: A PDF has no single DPI; each picture inside has its own. In Adobe Acrobat Pro, open Output Preview, choose Object Inspector and click a picture to see its resolution. Free option: divide the picture's pixel width by its printed width in inches. Print needs about 300 DPI.

body:
First: a PDF doesn't have "a" DPI

Text in a PDF prints sharp at any size, because it's made of shapes, not pixels. Only the pictures have a DPI, and each one can be different. A book can have a perfect cover photo and one blurry chart on page 112. So you're really checking each picture. New to the term? Read what DPI means.

Way 1: The simple math (free)

  1. Find the picture's size in pixels (right-click the original image file, then Properties or Get Info).
  2. Measure how wide it prints on the page, in inches.
  3. Divide: pixels ÷ inches = DPI. A 1,500-pixel-wide picture printed 5 inches wide is 300 DPI. Printed 6 inches wide, it's only 250.

Or skip the math: drop the picture into SparkPrep's free DPI checker, type the printed size, and it tells you the real DPI. It runs in your browser and never uploads the file.

Way 2: Adobe Acrobat Pro

  1. Open your PDF in Acrobat Pro and go to Print Production, then Output Preview.
  2. In the Preview menu, choose Object Inspector.
  3. Click a picture on the page. The panel shows its resolution in pixels per inch.

This works well, but you have to click every picture on every page, and Acrobat Pro is a paid program.

Way 3: Check the whole book at once

For a full book, clicking picture by picture is slow and easy to miss. SparkPrep is an Automated Publishing Production System (A.P.P.S.): upload the PDF and it checks every picture on every page and the cover, and lists the exact pages under 300 DPI.

The Word setting that lowers your DPI

If you made your book in Microsoft Word, Word may have shrunk your pictures without asking. Before you save your PDF:

  • Go to File, Options, Advanced, find Image Size and Quality.
  • Tick Do not compress images in file, and set the default resolution to High fidelity.
  • Then re-insert any pictures that were already shrunk, and save the PDF again. Steps: export a print-ready PDF from Word.

If a picture is too low

Use the original, larger file, or print the picture smaller. Making the number bigger in an app doesn't add detail. More fixes: how to fix low-resolution images. Not sure what size the page is? See the trim size chart.

faq.q: Can I check the DPI of a PDF for free?
faq.a: Yes. Divide each picture's pixel width by the inches it prints at, or use SparkPrep's free DPI checker on the original picture. To check every picture in a whole PDF at once, upload it to SparkPrep's book check.

faq.q: What DPI should a PDF be for printing a book?
faq.a: About 300 DPI for every picture at the size it prints, including the cover. Text doesn't have a DPI and prints sharp at any size.

faq.q: Why are my PDF pictures blurry when they looked fine in Word?
faq.a: Word compresses pictures by default when it saves. Turn on 'Do not compress images in file' under File, Options, Advanced, re-insert the pictures, and export the PDF again.
